title: Affine Fitting ideals and finite generators under arbitrary sheaf pullback
statement: Let $g:T\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $r\geq0$. Let $\mathcal G=g^*\mathcal F$ be the module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and use the Fitting ideal sheaves of [def-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf]. Then $\mathcal G$ is finite type and quasi-coherent. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ and affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq T$ with $g(V)\subseteq U$, let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the induced ring map and put $M=\mathcal F(U)$. There is an isomorphism $\mathcal G|_V\cong\widetilde{B\otimes_A M}$, with the associated sheaf notation of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Under the resulting identification of sections, any finite generating family $m_1,\ldots,m_n$ of $M$ maps to the generating family $1\otimes m_1,\ldots,1\otimes m_n$ of $B\otimes_A M$. If $I=\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)(U)=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)$, then $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)(V)=\operatorname{Fit}_r(B\otimes_A M)=\varphi(I)B$, where $\varphi(I)B$ is the ideal generated by the images of the elements of $I$ and module Fitting ideals are the presentation-independent kernel-minor ideals of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Consequently $\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal G)=g^{-1}\operatorname{Fit}_r(\mathcal F)\cdot\mathcal O_T$ as ideal subsheaves of $\mathcal O_T$. Neither flatness of $g$ nor finite presentation of $\mathcal F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0C3D, lemma-base-change-fitting-ideal, expanded into its affine tensor and finite-generation computation from the returned proof step 4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] to the given morphism $g$ and module $\mathcal F$. They show that $\mathcal G=g^*\mathcal F$ is finite type and quasi-coherent, without any condition on $g$. On each prescribed affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] shows that $M=\mathcal F(U)$ is finitely generated. Thus a finite generating surjection $\pi:A^n\twoheadrightarrow M$ exists; no finiteness of its kernel is asserted.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to the specified affine pair. Swap the tensor factors and use its second-factor scalar compatibility to obtain a B-linear bijection from B tensor_A F(U) to the sections of the actual tensor pullback. Its pure-tensor formula and the normalized unit formula of [def-pc-module-pullback] send 1 tensor m to the restricted actual tensorPullbackSection. For the sheaf isomorphism, restrict the quasi-coherent pullback to Spec B, apply the counit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], transport the module of sections by this B-linear equivalence and the canonical restriction-sections equivalence, and restrict back along V.isoSpec.hom.

Use the scalar-extension operation of [def-weil-module-base-change]. Mathlib Submodule.baseChange_span identifies the scalar extension of the span of a family with the B-span of its elements 1 tensor m. Apply this to the equality span_A(range m)=top and use Submodule.baseChange_top and Set.range_comp. This works for every finite family, including the empty one; in the ring-map algebra structure the tensor unit is exactly affinePullbackOneTensor.

For every given surjection pi, the affine source section ideal is its kernel-minor ideal by [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-affine-sections]. The base-change clause of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] gives both surjectivity of the base-changed presentation and extension of its kernel-minor ideal. Compose that presentation with the B-linear equivalence of step 2. Surjectivity is preserved. For each row x, e(pi_B(x))=0 if and only if pi_B(x)=0 because e is injective, so the defining sets of kernel-row determinants and hence the presentation ideals are identical, including the n<=r case. Apply [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf-affine-sections] to this composed presentation on V, then rewrite by that kernel-minor equality to obtain all displayed affine equalities.

proof.text: Apply the existing closed affine ideal formula [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension]: (Fit_r(F).comap g)(V) is Ideal.map (g.appLE U V) (Fit_r(F)(U)). On each such affine pair, choose a finite-free surjection onto F(U), which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], and combine the two equalities from step 4 to identify the two affine ideals. These V cover T: choose affine U around g(t), then affine V around t contained in g inverse U. Mathlib IdealSheafData.ext_of_iSup_eq_top turns equality on that affine cover into the global ideal-sheaf equality. No image-module construction, structure-sheaf pullback comparison or injectivity of a pulled-back ideal inclusion is needed.

lean.statement: theorem fittingSheaf_arbitrary_pullback {T S : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFiniteType] [F.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ) : ∃ (hft : ((tensorPullback g).obj F).IsFiniteType) (hqc : ((tensorPullback g).obj F).IsQuasicoherent), (∀ (U : S.affineOpens) (V : T.affineOpens) (h : V.1 ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ U.1), Nonempty (((tensorPullback g).obj F).restrict V.1.ι ≅ (tilde (affinePullbackTensor g F U V h)).restrict V.2.isoSpec.hom) ∧ ∃ e : affinePullbackTensor g F U V h ≃ₗ[Γ(T, V.1)] Γ((tensorPullback g).obj F, V.1), (∀ m : Γ(F, U.1), e (affinePullbackOneTensor g F U V h m) = ((tensorPullback g).obj F).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op (tensorPullbackSection g F U.1 m)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (m : Fin n → Γ(F, U.1)), Submodule.span Γ(S, U.1) (Set.range m) = ⊤ → Submodule.span Γ(T, V.1) (Set.range (fun i ↦ affinePullbackOneTensor g F U V h (m i))) = ⊤) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (π : (Fin n → Γ(S, U.1)) →ₗ[Γ(S, U.1)] Γ(F, U.1)), Function.Surjective π → (fittingIdealSheaf F r).ideal U = π.presentationFittingIdeal r ∧ Function.Surjective (affinePullbackPresentation g F U V h π) ∧ (@fittingIdealSheaf T ((tensorPullback g).obj F) hft hqc r).ideal V = (affinePullbackPresentation g F U V h π).presentationFittingIdeal r ∧ (affinePullbackPresentation g F U V h π).presentationFittingIdeal r = Ideal.map (g.appLE U.1 V.1 h).hom ((fittingIdealSheaf F r).ideal U))) ∧ @fittingIdealSheaf T ((tensorPullback g).obj F) hft hqc r = (fittingIdealSheaf F r).comap g
lean.note: Three transparent helper definitions specialize existing extension of scalars, its unit and LinearMap.baseChangePresentation to the induced affine section ring map. Finite-type and quasi-coherence witnesses are existentially bound so the Fitting ideal of the actual tensor pullback is well typed without adding preservation assumptions. Module Fitting ideals are rendered for every surjective finite-free presentation, using the recorded presentation-independent kernel-minor ideal; comap is the extended ideal subsheaf, not tensor pullback of the ideal inclusion.
